summary: Remove duplicates in place so each value appears at most twice; return the new length.
mainInsight: Keep a write index k. Process each element x; it may be written iff k < 2 or x != nums[k - 2]. Since the array is sorted, comparing with the element two positions behind the write index guarantees at most two copies of any value.

approaches.name: Counting duplicates with a counter
approaches.summary: Track the run length and write only if count <= 2.

approaches.name: Compare with nums[k - 2]
approaches.summary: Write when k < 2 or x != nums[k - 2].
strengths: Tiny and generalises to 'at most K'

commonMistakes: Starting k at 0 without the k < 2 guard
Comparing with the read element after it was overwritten

incorrectOptionExplanations.k < 2 or x != nums[k - 1]: That allows only one copy of each value.
incorrectOptionExplanations.x != nums[i - 2] using the read index: The original array has been overwritten.

promptVariants: Why compare with nums[k - 2] rather than the read pointer's previous element?
cards.answer: The write region nums[:k] is the valid output so far. If x equals nums[k - 2] and the array is sorted then nums[k - 1] is also equal to x, so adding x would create a third copy. For 'at most K copies' compare with nums[k - K].
keyPoints: Use nums[k - K] for K copies
cards.explanation: Comparing against read positions is unsafe since they may be overwritten.
